title: Streaming ZPA audit logs to a SIEM: log type, fields, filtering
aliases: stream zpa audit logs to splunk

prose.text: Audit logs are streamed by a log receiver of the Audit Logs type; the receiver mechanics are in [[zpa.log-receivers]].

prose.label: Fields.
prose.text: The field list was an open question until the field article was captured {{gap:field-schema}}. {{default-fields}} {{operation-values}} {{old-new-value}} {{object-fields}} {{client-audit-update}} {{custom-template}}

prose.label: Delivery.
prose.text: The audit-log exception to the loss behavior is in [[zpa.app-connectors.health]]; what the exception means is open {{gap:audit-recovery-mechanism}}.

prose.label: Filtering.
prose.text: {{no-audit-status-filter}} {{no-audit-policy-rule}} [[zpa.log-receivers.filtering:siem-policy-set]] What the API itself accepts for an audit-log receiver is open {{gap:audit-filter-api}} {{gap:siem-policy-purpose}}.

prose.label: Microtenants.
prose.text: {{disabled-microtenant-audit-only}} Audit Logs of the Default Microtenant are not visible to a Microtenant admin [[zpa.microtenants.admin-permissions]], and deleting a Microtenant deletes the log receivers it is associated with [[zpa.microtenants.lifecycle]]. How a microtenant's own audit entries are scoped between it and its parent is open {{gap:microtenant-scoping}}.

checks.do: That the receiver's log type is Audit Logs (source log type zpn_audit_log) rather than User Activity.
Which fields the receiver's stream content includes, against the default field list, if a custom template was saved.
Whether the entry is a change or a session event from auditOperationType, and which of auditOldValue or auditNewValue applies.
That no status-code filter or streaming policy is expected to narrow an audit-log receiver.
Whether a gap in the SIEM data coincides with a connection loss, and that the audit-log exception is not described further.
Whether microtenants are enabled on the receiver when a microtenant's audit entries are missing, and which microtenant the admin belongs to.

audit-log-type.statement: The Audit Logs log type carries session information for all admins accessing the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: Audit Logs: Session information for all admins accessing the Zscaler Admin Console.

audit-source-type.statement: A log receiver's source log type for audit logs is `zpn_audit_log`; the Python SDK reaches it through the `audit_logs` key.

quotes: zpn_audit_log: Denotes the Audit Log log type.
evidence.after: The log type of the LSS resource. The supported values are:

quotes: "audit_logs": "zpn_audit_log",

default-fields.statement: By default the audit stream carries thirteen fields in each template (CSV, JSON, TSV): modifiedTime, creationTime, modifiedBy, requestID, auditOldValue, auditNewValue, auditOperationType, objectType, objectName, objectID, customerID, modifiedByUser and clientAuditUpdate.

quotes: By default, the audit log type includes the fields listed in the table below for each log template (i.e., CSV, JSON, TSV).
| modifiedTime | The time when an object is created, deleted, or updated |
| creationTime | The time when the log was generated |
| modifiedBy | The user ID for the admin that made the change |
| requestID | The ID for the associated configuration change, as related to the action that was made |
| auditOldValue | The previous value that was changed if the action type is delete, sign out, or update.
| auditNewValue | The new value that was changed if the action type is create, sign in, or update.
| auditOperationType | The action performed.
| objectType | The location within the Zscaler Admin Console where the Action was performed.
| objectName | The name of the object. This corresponds to the Resource Name on the Audit Log page.
| objectID | The ID associated with the object name |
| customerID | The Private Access tenant ID of the customer.
| modifiedByUser | The username of the admin associated with the audit action |
| clientAuditUpdate | Indicates whether the logs are associated with admin or client credentials.

operation-values.statement: auditOperationType takes Create, Client Session Revoked, Delete, Download, Sign In, Sign In Failure, Sign Out and Update; the Nonce MaxUsage Increment action of the console is not listed for this field.

quotes: The action performed.The expected values for this field:CreateClient Session RevokedDeleteDownloadSign InSign In FailureSign OutUpdate

old-new-value.statement: auditOldValue holds the previous value when the action is delete, sign out or update, and auditNewValue holds the new value when the action is create, sign in or update; for a policy object the value is Allow for an access policy, Intercept for a client forwarding policy and Re_Auth for a timeout policy.

quotes: The previous value that was changed if the action type is delete, sign out, or update.
The new value that was changed if the action type is create, sign in, or update.
Allow: the policy type is access policyIntercept: the policy type is client forwarding policyRe_Auth: the policy type is timeout policy
evidence.after: The previous value that was changed if the action type is delete, sign out, or update.

object-fields.statement: objectType is the location in the Admin Console where the action was performed and corresponds to the Resource Type on the Audit Log page; objectName corresponds to the Resource Name.

quotes: The location within the Zscaler Admin Console where the Action was performed. This corresponds to the Resource Type on the Audit Log page.
The name of the object. This corresponds to the Resource Name on the Audit Log page.

client-audit-update.statement: clientAuditUpdate indicates whether the entry is associated with admin or client credentials, with expected values 0 and 1.

quotes: Indicates whether the logs are associated with admin or client credentials. The expected values for this field are 0 and 1.

custom-template.statement: While configuring the log receiver the default log stream content can be edited to capture only specific fields, which creates a Custom log template.

quotes: While configuring your log receiver, you can edit the default log stream content to capture only specific fields, and create a Custom log template.

no-audit-status-filter.statement: The Terraform provider rejects a status-code filter on a `zpn_audit_log` receiver, and the documented status-codes response lists codes only for the User Status, App Connector Status, User Activity and Private Service Edge Status log types.

quotes: "zpn_audit_log": "Audit Logs",
return fmt.Errorf("filter is not supported for source log type %s - %s", sourceLogType, displayName)
- "zpn_ast_auth_log": {
- "zpn_sys_auth_log": {

no-audit-status-filter.conditions: Provider behavior plus an absence in an example response: the status-codes example in the API article shows four top-level log types and none for audit logs. What the server does with a filter sent directly is not shown (see gap audit-filter-api).

no-audit-policy-rule.statement: The Terraform provider accepts policy rule operands only on User Status and User Activity receivers and returns an invalid-source-log-type error for any other source log type, which includes `zpn_audit_log`.

quotes: validObjectTypes = validObjectTypesForAuthLog
validObjectTypes = validObjectTypesForTransLog
return fmt.Errorf("invalid source_log_type: %s", sourceLogType)

no-audit-policy-rule.conditions: Reading the object-type switch in validateLSSConfigControllerFilters: the cases are zpn_auth_log and zpn_trans_log and the default returns the error. This is the client's validation, not the server's.

disabled-microtenant-audit-only.statement: On a log receiver, when a Microtenant is disabled only audit logs are streamed for it, and all Microtenants are selected by default when the receiver is configured in the Default Microtenant.

quotes: If a Microtenant is disabled, then only audit logs are streamed to the log receiver.
All Microtenants are selected by default if you are configuring a log receiver within the Default Microtenant.

field-schema.title: Fields of a zpn_audit_log stream entry
field-schema.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-32: the specific fields present in a zpn_audit_log LSS stream entry were not captured.
field-schema.resolution: The Understanding Audit Log Fields article is captured and lists the default fields; see claim default-fields.

audit-recovery-mechanism.title: What the audit-log exception to the loss behavior does
audit-recovery-mechanism.detail: The help says that, with the exception of audit log data, LSS transmits nothing generated during a connection loss between the App Connector and the SIEM. It does not say what happens to audit log data during such a loss, how long it is held, or whether the 15-minute retransmit applies. Unverified legacy statement: "After a connection is restored, the LSS can retransmit the last 15 minutes of audit log data." The legacy wording attributes the retransmit to the audit-log case; the source attaches the 15 minutes to the loss between Private Access and the App Connectors.

audit-filter-api.title: Whether the API accepts a filter on an audit-log receiver
audit-filter-api.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-35. The Terraform provider rejects any filter on a `zpn_audit_log` receiver and the documented status-codes response has no audit-log entry (no-audit-status-filter), which answers the valid-expression question for the provider. Whether the server rejects, ignores or accepts a filter on this log type when called directly is not shown.

siem-policy-purpose.title: Whether a SIEM policy rule can narrow an audit-log stream
siem-policy-purpose.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-33. The SDK says SIEM_POLICY is the parent policy set of a receiver's policy rule (siem-policy-set), and the provider accepts policy operands only for User Status and User Activity (no-audit-policy-rule). Whether the API applies a policy rule to an audit-log receiver, and what the unused `zpa_policy_type` SIEM_POLICY lookup in the provider's audit-log example is for, are not shown.

microtenant-scoping.title: Whether a microtenant's audit entries are isolated or visible to the parent
microtenant-scoping.detail: Tracked as legacy ledger item zpa-34. The help ties audit streaming to the microtenant selection on a receiver (disabled-microtenant-audit-only), and the microtenant subjects source that the Default Microtenant's Audit Logs are not visible to a Microtenant admin; no source says whether the audit logs of a microtenant stream only through that microtenant's receivers or also through the parent's.
